title.en: Vegetative, asexual and sexual reproduction in plants, and the flower

text.en: Put a Bryophyllum leaf on damp soil and tiny plantlets sprout from its notches. No seeds, no flowers - yet new plants appear. That is one of three ways plants reproduce.

Reproduction ensures continuity of the species. Plants reproduce in three ways: vegetative, asexual and sexual.
In vegetative reproduction a detached vegetative part (root, stem, leaf or bud) grows into a new plant by mitosis only, so the offspring are genetically similar to the parent.
Examples: Bryophyllum leaf notches, strawberry runners, tuberous roots of sweet potato and asparagus, and bulbils of Agave.
Other methods: fragmentation in Spirogyra, fission in Amoeba, budding in yeast and regeneration in Hydra and Planaria.
Asexual reproduction is by a single parent without gametes, as by spores formed in the sporangium of Rhizopus; the offspring are exact copies.
Sexual reproduction needs fusion of male and female gametes; a flower is a modified shoot with four whorls: calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium.
Calyx and corolla are accessory whorls, while androecium and gynoecium are essential whorls.
The stamen has a filament and an anther producing pollen; the pistil has a stigma, style and ovary with ovules.
A pollen grain has an outer hard exine with germ pores and a thin inner intine; it holds a vegetative cell and a generative cell, which divides into two male gametes.
The ovule has a nucellus covered by two integuments with a micropyle; its embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei: egg apparatus of three cells, three antipodal cells and two polar nuclei.

problem.en: Is a plant grown from a potato tuber a result of sexual or vegetative reproduction? Is it identical to the parent?

text.en: A tuber is a vegetative part of the plant.
So it is vegetative reproduction by mitosis.
The new plant is genetically similar to the parent.

prompt.en: Name the four whorls of a flower from the outside and say which are essential.

points.en: Vegetative: from roots, stems, leaves or buds; offspring similar to parent.
Asexual: single parent, by spores; sexual: fusion of gametes.
Embryo sac has 7 cells and 8 nuclei.
